Too costly relative to other brands for now, not a data-quality problem.

name: New Works DK
notes: Un-deferred 2026-09-11 - rechecked at the user's prompt after being deferred on 2026-09-07 for a client-rendered Nuxt SPA. That's no longer true: the site now server-renders its full 150-item /en/shop grid directly (name, material/color, price, real ). Same color-variant-as-separate-listing pattern as several other brands (e.g. 'Rand Side Table' has 2 separate URLs, one per finish) - grouped by exact name with color folded into material_options. 85 real products after grouping. No category signal on the listing itself, left blank rather than fetching all 150 product pages just for that.

name: Baleri Italia
notes: Custom AJAX products.json (returns an HTML fragment, not structured JSON). Its page param is silently ignored - every page number returns the same first 24 products, and hasMorePages is always true regardless - so only that single reliable page is scraped. Real catalog is almost certainly larger; ~24 products is a known partial-coverage limitation, not a bug.

notes: Real /collections/all product page.

notes: robots.txt gives ClaudeBot (and GPTBot, Google-Extended, etc.) its own dedicated 'Disallow: /' record, separate from the general wildcard rule - a specific, deliberate exclusion, same pattern as Atelier de Troupe/Bennet Schlesinger. Also behind Cloudflare bot-management (sitemap.xml itself returns a JS challenge page) - same wall as Nikari. Excluded on either signal alone; both together confirm it.

name: Ingo Maurer
notes: robots.txt allows everything, no bot-specific blocks. No product API, but /en/products/ server-renders the full catalog (266 items, name+image+link) in one fetch - same shape as H. Bigeleisen/Yird Ceramics. ~129 of 266 are marked Discontinued Models (pc10/is-ceased class) and excluded.

name: Källemo
notes: Joomla site, generic robots.txt (no bot-specific blocks). No product API, but 6 category listing pages under /en/products/{category} each server-render every item's name, designer, and image in one fetch. A 7th category, 'archive', is discontinued designs and is excluded, same treatment as Ingo Maurer's ceased models. Category label set per-folder where unambiguous (chairs/tables/shelves), left blank where a folder genuinely mixes object types (sofas-easychairs, other, limited).

name: Mizuyo
notes: robots.txt is the generic Squarespace AI-bot template (harmless, same as H. Bigeleisen/Yird), not a real block. Deferred for a different reason: the /shop listing has zero products in its server-rendered HTML (no product markup or embedded JSON - likely client-fetched or currently empty), and individual product pages (checked /kasuri-apron, /kiriko) only carry generic site-level schema.org data, no per-product name/price/image. Most of the rest of the site is one-off named Kintsugi client commissions and repair supplies, not shop-able design objects. Real working London ceramicist (Mizuyo Yamashita), but nothing structured to scrape right now - worth rechecking later in case a real shop catalog appears.

name: Studio Racines
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront with a robots.txt that explicitly allows crawling (no bot-specific block) - but the whole site is currently behind Shopify's password/coming-soon gate (homepage and /collections/all both redirect to 'Enter using password', /products.json returns 401). Nothing public to scrape yet. Not excluded, just not launched - recheck once it's live.

name: e15
notes: robots.txt itself is permissive (no bot-specific block, just generic WP-admin/downloads/sample-sale exclusions). Magento catalog, real per-product data confirmed (its /en/all-products.html?limit=all listing briefly returned all 141 products with clean name/category/image in one fetch). But real bot-mitigation infrastructure kicked in during testing - the same URLs (and eventually the homepage too) started returning 403 consistently, including for a plain browser user-agent and curl, not just this scraper's own UA. Same treatment as Nikari's Cloudflare wall: not routed around.

name: De La Espada
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront, robots.txt allows crawling (Shopify's standard agentic-commerce template, no bot-specific block). 349 clean products across real categories (Sofas, Storage, Dining Chairs, etc.), no junk/sample/swatch categories found, all 349 have images - uses the existing generic extract_shopify unmodified. One small known gap: 8 of 349 products (2.3%) use ' - ' as part of their real name (e.g. 'TAI HEN - BOOKSHELF') rather than as a variant separator, so _base_name() truncates the descriptive suffix on display - not a merging/duplication bug, just a shortened name on a handful of cards.

name: Elliott Denny
notes: robots.txt blocks everything for every user-agent (User-agent: * / Disallow: /) - a blanket site-wide block including search engines, not just AI/bot crawlers. Clearest possible exclusion signal, no further checks needed.

name: Piet Hein Eek
notes: Real WooCommerce store, robots.txt is generic Yoast/WP boilerplate (no bot block). 1,141 raw products across 12 pages, uses the existing generic extract_woocommerce. Real per-brand quirk found and handled: several categories ('Architectuur', 'Architectuur projecten', 'Inrichtingen', 'Horeca', ~50-60 items) are real architecture/interior-fit-out case studies (hospitality venues, private homes), not purchasable furniture - confirmed all price=0 and added to EXCLUDED_CATEGORIES. Note most of the REAL flagship scrapwood ('Sloophout') pieces are also price=0 (priced on request, common for one-of-a-kind artisanal furniture) - price alone isn't a reliable signal here, category is. The much broader 'Opdrachten' (commissions) category was deliberately left alone - it mixes those same project writeups with genuinely real bespoke furniture, too broad to exclude cleanly.

name: Joris Poggioli
notes: No robots.txt file exists at all (site returns its own 404 page for the path) - no bot restrictions of any kind. Next.js app whose homepage server-renders its entire 74-item design catalog directly in a __NEXT_DATA__ JSON blob - name, category, material, dimensions, and image all present, no per-product fetch needed. The site's separate 'architecture' section (real interior/hospitality project case studies) isn't part of this data at all, so nothing to exclude.

name: Moustache
notes: PrestaShop store, generic robots.txt (no bot block). Real structural complexity found and handled: the site runs two parallel, near-non-overlapping category URL trees under /en/ (an older French-slugged one and a newer English-slugged one, most likely because English URL slugs were only set on newer categories) - no single 'all products' listing actually covers everything (its 86-all category is itself just a distinct 54-item subset). extract_moustache() fetches every real object-type category from both trees and dedupes by PrestaShop's own numeric product ID. Also found: each color is its own top-level product (confirmed live - 'Gelato chair' alone had 42 separate IDs, one per color, with the color name only appearing in the product URL's fragment, not the visible name) - 78% of the raw 444-item catalog was this pattern. Grouped by exact product name with colors parsed from the URL fragment into material_options, same treatment as every other brand's variant-duplication problem. 157 real products after grouping.

name: Buro Berger
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront, robots.txt permissive (no bot block). 52 products, all with images, real categories (Candle Holder, Tableware, Small Furniture). Uses the existing generic extract_shopify unmodified.

name: Silcohaus
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront, robots.txt permissive. Small catalog (6 products) but real, all with images, real categories (Furniture, Lamp). Describes itself as a 'curation platform' rather than a single maker/manufacturer - worth rechecking later whether it's genuinely its own line or a multi-brand reseller, but its own products.json only returns 6 items regardless. Uses the existing generic extract_shopify unmodified.

name: Designbythem
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront, robots.txt permissive. 287 raw products, 36 are 'Swatches' (already in EXCLUDED_CATEGORIES, auto-excluded) - rest are real furniture categories (Modular Sofas, Chairs, Dining Tables, etc.), all with images. Uses the existing generic extract_shopify unmodified.

name: Raawii
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront, robots.txt permissive. Real categories (Lounge chair, Bench, Bar Stool, Mirror, Table, Ottoman), all with images. Uses the existing generic extract_shopify unmodified.

name: Utilitario Mexicano
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront, robots.txt permissive. Categories are Spanish material/type words (CANTERAS/quarry-stone, ESMALTADOS/enameled, PIELES/leather, etc.) rather than object-type categories - same shape as Bitossi's collection-line gap, a known limitation not a bug. Real junk found and excluded: 'editorial' (books/magazines), 'musica' (vinyl records), 'operativo' (a gift-card listing) - same 'Libri fisici' shape as Bitossi, just Spanish category names. All remaining products have images. Uses the existing generic extract_shopify unmodified.

name: Galvin Brothers
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront, robots.txt permissive. 97 products, real furniture categories (Side Table, Dining Table, Stool, Sideboard, Chair, Bench, etc.), one 'Care Kit' listing (furniture maintenance kit, not a design object - added to EXCLUDED_CATEGORIES). Uses the existing generic extract_shopify unmodified.

name: Mati Sipiora
notes: Genuine WooCommerce store, robots.txt generic WP boilerplate (no bot block). Small catalog (13 products) but real, all with images, real categories (Seating, Accessories, Storage). Solo designer/craftsman working within his family's metalworking workshop in Poland. Uses the existing generic extract_woocommerce unmodified.

name: Patrick de Glo de Besses
notes: His own portfolio site (patrickdeglodebesses.com) only works over plain http (broken TLS on https) and isn't the shop anyway - the real shop is on Big Cartel, which exposes a clean public /products.json (no robots.txt block). 15 real chair sculptures, all with images. New generic extract_bigcartel() built for this - Big Cartel is a real, reusable platform (also recommended on the resources page for makers), not a one-off.

name: B-Line Italia
notes: No product API, robots.txt permissive (empty/no restrictions). Its /en/prodotti/ listing server-renders the full 20-item catalog (name + image) in one fetch - a real, established Italian design-icon reissue brand (Joe Colombo's Boby trolley). No category on the listing itself, left blank rather than fetching all 20 product pages just for that.

name: Omelette Editions
notes: WordPress/WooCommerce, but the Store API isn't exposed and there's no single listing page with the full catalog (/en/productos/ itself shows category tiles, not products). The site's own SEO sitemap (productos-sitemap.xml) is the only place the 37 real per-product URLs are enumerated - fetches that, keeps only the English-language URLs (dropping parallel Spanish duplicates), then fetches each product page directly for name/image via og:title/og:image. Category comes from the URL path segment (translated where Spanish, e.g. butacas->Armchair) rather than a per-page fetch.

name: Par en Par
notes: Not to be confused with the unrelated US resort-wear apparel brand at the plain .com domain of the same name - this is a genuinely different, real furniture/lighting/ceramics maker in Argentina (user provided the correct .com.ar URL after the initial search surfaced the wrong brand). Runs on Tiendanube (a Latin American e-commerce platform), no Shopify-style products.json exposed, so this fetches the platform's own gzipped sitemap (its location comes straight from robots.txt's Sitemap: line) for real product URLs, then each product page's WebPage JSON-LD breadcrumb for name/category and og:image for the photo. 62 of 80 sitemap URLs resolved (rest are stale/discontinued, cleanly skipped on 404). Known minor noise: a few products pick up a marketing-campaign breadcrumb instead of a clean category (e.g. 'Experiencia Living | Lanzamiento NEXO') - not a correctness bug, just unhelpful for category search matching on those specific items.

name: Łukasz Korol
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront, robots.txt permissive (Shopify's standard agentic-commerce template, no ClaudeBot-specific block - unlike the wrong domain initially found for this designer). 9 real solid-wood furniture products (Polish names - Kredens z jesionu/ash cabinet, Biurko z jawora/maple desk, etc.), all with images. Uses the existing generic extract_shopify unmodified.

name: Eric Schmitt Studio
notes: Real official site exists after all (user provided the correct URL - initial search only found gallery pages, not this). Dated custom/PHP site, robots.txt fully permissive. No product API, but each of 13 real category listing pages (/realisations_{slug}) server-renders every item's name, designer credit, and image in one fetch - no per-product fetch needed. Deliberately excludes the parallel 'editeurs_*' category pages (same objects re-grouped by which gallery represents them - Carpenters Workshop, Ralph Pucci, Galerie Dutko, etc. - would just duplicate everything) and 'in-situ'/'projets' (installation photography, not standalone objects). 385 real products across a long, prolific career - Eric Schmitt is a well-established French designer/sculptor (b. 1955), represented by major galleries.

name: Hadaki
notes: Confirmed same brand at the corrected URL (New Orleans-based travel bags/luggage accessories) - out of Formground's category scope (furniture/lighting/ceramics/objects) regardless. Also independently blocked: robots.txt gives ClaudeBot/GPTBot their own dedicated 'Disallow: /' via the same Cloudflare Content-Signal template as Driade/Toou/Bomma. Excluded on either signal alone.

name: Eine Kleine Furniture
notes: A genuinely old, tiny site (1990s-style HTML frameset, no real robots.txt - the request 404s at the host level) for a small Seoul-based white-oak furniture maker - exactly the smallest/least-resourced tier this project targets. Real catalog runs on a Korean forum/board CMS (Gnuboard-style) split across two boards ('original' ready-made, 'order_made' custom) - each listing page already server-renders every item's name (a bare product code, e.g. 'EKBS-01' - the site's own naming convention, same shape as Joris Poggioli's numbered pieces) and thumbnail as a pair of same-wr_id <a> tags, no per-post fetch needed. 36 real products, all with images.

name: Jon Goulder
notes: Squarespace site (Australia, Avoca Beach). robots.txt lists ClaudeBot/GPTBot in named blocks with no Disallow under them - the harmless generic template also seen on Dan Mack Studio and Jackie Wright Ceramics, not the real Content-Signal block used by Driade/Toou/Bomma/Hadaki. The /work-furniture-objects-lighting listing server-renders images/links for all 17 real products but no visible name text, so each product page is fetched once for its <title> (prefixed "Jon Goulder " - stripped) while the listing image is reused. No category signal on the listing, left blank (same tradeoff as B-Line Italia/H. Bigeleisen).

name: La Chambre d'Ami
notes: Wix Stores site (France) with a real store-products-sitemap.xml and server-rendered schema.org Product JSON-LD (name, image) on every /product-page/ URL - reliable despite Wix's reputation for client-rendered storefronts. 60 sitemap entries, 9 skipped as consumables/accessories rather than design objects (room-fragrance refills/samples, a bare lightbulb, a generic electrical fitting, a tote bag) via a hardcoded skip list since there's no category field to filter on generically. No price/category on the remaining ~51 real products (color is a buyer-chosen option, not a fixed attribute).

name: Esther Knopfler
notes: Wix Portfolio site for a sculptural marble furniture designer. portfolio-projects-sitemap.xml lists all 24 pieces cleanly (checked: no junk/consumables, unlike La Chambre d'Ami) as /portfolio-collections/{collection}/{slug}. Each page server-renders og:title/og:image. The collection segment in the URL doubles as a free category (e.g. "burger-collection" -> "Burger Collection") at no extra fetch cost.

name: Mercoeur Editions
notes: Webflow site for a French design publishing house. /all-products server-renders name, link, and image for the full 18-item catalog in one fetch - no per-product pages needed. No reliable category signal (slug/display-name word order disagree), left blank.

name: DE VORM
notes: Next.js site (Netherlands) - the product catalog is client-rendered (empty on initial HTML fetch, populated by JS after load), no public product API found. Not worth the headless-browser tradeoff for one brand's catalog.

name: The Horang
notes: Imweb (Korean SaaS platform) storefront - client-rendered SPA shell, no catalog content in the initial HTML and no public product API found. robots.txt itself is permissive (only disallows /site_join), so this is a rendering limitation, not a bot block.

name: Volker Haug Studio
notes: Nuxt.js site (Australia) explicitly configured with serverRendered:false in its own page config - confirmed client-side-only rendering, no catalog in the initial HTML and no public product API found.

name: Dan Mack Studio
notes: Squarespace site - the product grid itself is client-rendered (not present in the initial HTML), and the usual Squarespace ?format=json fallback used elsewhere in this project is explicitly disallowed by this store's own robots.txt (Disallow: /search covers the format=json pattern here). robots.txt otherwise uses the harmless generic AI-bot-listing template (not a real ClaudeBot/GPTBot block).

name: Monsieur Cailloux
notes: Webflow site (France) - the collection/cart template renders products client-side via JS, nothing in the initial HTML and no public product API found.

name: Arkadiusz Szwed
notes: Cargo.site portfolio - an unstructured freeform collage/scroll layout with no consistent product markup (no repeated card/listing structure to key an extractor off), unreliable to parse without a lot of one-off logic for a single small maker's page.

name: Jackie Wright Ceramics
notes: Squarespace site (UK) - the shop is behind a password gate, nothing public to scrape. robots.txt uses the harmless generic AI-bot-listing template (not a real ClaudeBot/GPTBot block), so the password gate is the actual blocker.

name: Toou
notes: Blocked: robots.txt gives ClaudeBot and GPTBot their own dedicated 'Disallow: /' block via Shopify's Content-Signal template - the real blocking pattern (same as Driade/Bomma/Hadaki), not the harmless generic AI-bot-listing template. Respected, not worked around.

name: Bomma
notes: Blocked: robots.txt gives ClaudeBot and GPTBot their own dedicated 'Disallow: /' block via Shopify's Content-Signal template - the real blocking pattern (same as Driade/Toou/Hadaki), not the harmless generic AI-bot-listing template. Respected, not worked around.

name: Libon Furniture
notes: Vite/React SPA (Egypt) - empty <div id="root"> on initial HTML fetch, no catalog content server-rendered and no public product API found in the JS bundle.

name: Black Pepper Paperie Co
notes: Genuine Shopify storefront with a permissive robots.txt, but the catalog (83 products) is overwhelmingly jewelry and apparel - only a small ceramics subset (~25 items) is in Formground's category scope, and this project scrapes a brand's real catalog rather than a hand-picked subset of it. Excluded as a scope mismatch rather than a technical block; worth revisiting if the ceramics line becomes its own storefront or grows to dominate the catalog.
